question: What did droplets of heptane fuel do aboard the space station after their flames went out?
answer: Many kept burning, unseen. In NASA's FLEX experiment, one large droplet's bright flame died, yet the droplet went on shrinking steadily: a cool flame, a slower reaction hundreds of degrees cooler and too dim for the eye, had taken over. On Earth such flames are fleeting; in weightlessness they held.
move: When the visible sign stops, check whether the process has stopped too.
source: Nayagam et al., Combustion and Flame, 2012
reference: Nayagam, Dietrich, Ferkul, Hicks & Williams, Can cool flames support quasi-steady alkane droplet burning?, Combustion and Flame, 2012
